deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a page of an administrative expert report (Gutachten), presumably drafted by Göttingen professors including Riemann. The report answers the Royal Hanoverian Curatorium about General J. J. Baeyer's proposal of 1861 for a Central European arc measurement (Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung).

Content of the page:
(a) The Curatorium has said that no new triangulation is intended. It wants only further scientific conclusions about the exact figure of the Earth drawn from the existing material of the Hanoverian arc measurement (Gauss's Gradmessung), and it asks for an opinion on this.
(b) The authors reply that this higher scientific aim will be fully reached once joint efforts have produced and published the necessary foundations:
  1) connected (contiguous) triangulations;
  2) completed and refined astronomical latitude and longitude determinations;
  3) equally systematic gravity (pendulum) determinations, added 'according to what is said in the Anlage'.
(c) Drawing all rigorous consequences from these foundations is an indivisible, purely scientific task. Whoever undertakes it must have full freedom. Good advice is admissible, but binding instructions are not, so nobody should be officially charged with 'directing' such work.

The next page completes the argument. The most useful thing Hanover can do is publish the results of the Hanoverian arc measurement fully, so that anyone can work on them. The report also recommends telegraphic longitude determinations by Klinkerfues. A pencil marginal note quotes Gauss's 'Bestimmung des Breitenunterschiedes zwischen den Sternwarten von Göttingen und Altona' (1828), Art. 20, on linking triangulations into one large system.

Scientifically, the substance is the methodological view that the figure of the Earth (the geoid) should be determined from three data types: geometric (triangulation), astronomical (latitude and longitude, i.e. deflections of the vertical) and gravimetric. This is a standard program in geodesy, going back to Clairaut, Laplace, Gauss/Bessel and Stokes (1849), and implemented later by Baeyer's organisation and Helmert. A pencil vertical line in the left margin marks the passage, and there are pencil interlinear insertions.

results.what: Programmatic statement: an accurate figure of the Earth requires connected triangulations, refined astronomical latitude/longitude determinations, and systematic gravity measurements, all published openly.
results.modern_name: Combined geometric-astronomical-gravimetric determination of the geoid (physical geodesy program; basis of the Mitteleuropäische / Europäische Gradmessung, later the International Association of Geodesy)
results.usually_credited_to: Baeyer (1861 memorandum 'Über die Grösse und Figur der Erde'); theoretical background from Clairaut (1743), Gauss (1828), Bessel, Stokes (1849); later systematised by Helmert (1880-84)

results.what: Science-policy recommendation: the theoretical evaluation of geodetic data should be left to free individual scholarship rather than directed by an appointed head; the state should publish the raw results of the Hanoverian Gradmessung.
results.modern_name: Open publication of scientific data / academic freedom argument in a science-policy report

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an administrative report on the Baeyer arc-measurement initiative and contains no mathematics. Riemann's participation in Göttingen faculty reports of this kind is plausible and of only minor biographical interest. Adding gravity determinations as a third foundation of geoid determination was already standard (Clairaut, Stokes, Bessel's pendulum work), and Baeyer's program itself discussed it.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear insertion above 'wissenschaftliche Zweck' reads more plausibly as 'dereinst' ('dieser höhere wissenschaftliche Zweck dereinst vollständig erreicht wird') than as 'dieser bei[?]'.

The pencil insertion below 'zu allgemeiner Kenntniß' ('den durch das vorhandene Material gegeben[...]') is partly struck through in the image, apparently at 'Material'. Its exact reading and placement are uncertain.
A pencil vertical line in the left margin runs from roughly 'dieser höhere...' to '...Bestimmungen'. This marks the passage and was not noted in the transcription.
'Es kann unserer Ansicht nicht fehlen' is hard to read in the image. 'unserem Erachten' or a similar phrase is possible, but the sense is unchanged.
The underlinings of 'höhere wissenschaftliche Zweck', 'Grundlagen' and 'Leitung' visible in the image are not marked in the transcription.
